examples.en: At dawn the fishing boats headed out to sea.

examples.ko: 항구에는 어선 수십 척이 묶여 있어요.
examples.en: Dozens of fishing boats are moored in the harbor.

examples.ko: 큰 파도 때문에 어선이 돌아오지 못했어요.
examples.en: The fishing boat couldn't return because of the big waves.

examples.ko: 어선 선장님이 그날 잡은 생선을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The captain of the fishing boat showed us the fish he caught that day.
We went to the island on a fishing boat.

examples.ko: 어선 한 척이 그물을 끌어 올리고 있어요.
examples.en: A fishing boat is hauling up its net.

explain: 고기를 잡는 배가 '어선', 사람을 태우는 배는 '여객선', 짐을 나르는 배는 '화물선'이에요. 배를 세는 단위는 '척'이라 '어선 한 척'이라고 해요. 낚시꾼을 태우는 작은 배는 '낚싯배'라고 따로 불러요.

phrases.example: 어선 한 척이 천천히 항구로 들어와요.
phrases.en: One fishing boat slowly comes into the port.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배를 세는 단위 '척'을 붙여 배의 수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the counter '척' to say how many boats there are.

phrases.en: The fishing boats go out to sea at dawn.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어선'과 뜻이 같지만 더 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '어선' but easier and more everyday.

phrases.en: My father works on a fishing boat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어선에 타서 일하거나 이동한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone rides or works on a fishing boat.

explain_en: Sino-Korean, neutral; boats used for fishing as work. A boat for catching fish is '어선'; one carrying passengers is '여객선', and one carrying cargo is '화물선'. Boats are counted with '척', so you say '어선 한 척'. A small boat that takes anglers out is called '낚싯배'.

t90.ax: A fishing boat is hauling up its net.

examples.ko: 배달용 이륜차는 인도로 다니면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Delivery two-wheelers must not ride on the sidewalk.

examples.ko: 이륜차를 탈 때는 꼭 헬멧을 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear a helmet when riding a two-wheeler.
Two-wheeler accidents increased, so enforcement was tightened.

examples.ko: 이륜차 전용 주차 구역이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A new parking area just for two-wheelers has been created.
My father works at a two-wheeler repair shop.

examples.ko: 오토바이나 스쿠터 같은 이륜차는 길에서 특히 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You need to be extra careful on the road with two-wheelers like motorcycles and scooters.

explain: 뉴스나 안내문에서 오토바이를 가리킬 때 많이 써서 '이륜차 사고', '이륜차 단속'처럼 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '오토바이'라고 해요. 자전거는 보통 따로 '자전거'라고 불러요.

phrases.en: I go to work on a motorcycle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 이륜차보다 이 말을 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Far more common than 이륜차 in everyday talk.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날에는 이륜차 사고가 늘어요.
phrases.en: Two-wheeler accidents increase on rainy days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 딱딱한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal collocation often heard in the news.

phrases.example: 이륜차 운전자는 안전모를 꼭 써야 해요.
phrases.en: Two-wheeler riders must wear a helmet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 규칙에서 운전하는 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices and rules for the person driving.

explain_en: In news and notices it is often used for motorcycles, as in '이륜차 사고' and '이륜차 단속'. In daily talk people just say '오토바이'. Bicycles are usually just called '자전거'.

examples.en: The amusement park has many kinds of rides.
Children like toy vehicles.
Buses, subways and taxis are all vehicles.
On this island there's nothing to ride but bicycles.
Which ride was the most fun?

examples.ko: 탈것을 이용할 때는 안전이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: Safety matters most when you use any vehicle.

explain: 버스, 기차, 자전거처럼 사람이 타는 것을 두루 말해요. 뉴스나 설명문에서는 '교통수단'을 많이 쓰고, '탈것'은 아이들 이야기나 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 써요. 놀이공원에서 타는 것은 '놀이기구'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Transportation in Seoul is convenient.
phrases.nuance_ko: '탈것'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스나 설명문에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: More formal than '탈것'; suits news and explanations.

phrases.en: I rode a scary ride at the amusement park.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이공원에서 타는 탈것만 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers only to rides at an amusement park.

phrases.en: Many kinds of vehicles appear in the picture book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 버스, 기차, 배처럼 종류가 다양하다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense of many kinds, like buses, trains, and boats.

explain_en: Plain-language, kids' word — anything you ride, like bikes or buses. It covers anything people ride, such as buses, trains and bicycles. News and explanatory texts prefer '교통수단', while '탈것' is more casual, often used in talk about children. Amusement park rides are also called '놀이기구'.

examples.en: Busan is a city with a large port.
There are many ships loaded with containers at the port.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 항만이 하루 동안 닫혔어요.
examples.en: The port was closed for a day because of the typhoon.
Port workers start working early in the morning.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 항만 시설을 새로 짓고 있어요.
examples.en: This country is building new port facilities.

examples.ko: 항만과 철도가 연결되어 물건을 빨리 옮겨요.
examples.en: With the port and railway connected, goods move quickly.

explain: '항만'은 배가 드나들고 짐을 싣고 내리는 시설을 통틀어 부르는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '항구'를 더 많이 말하고, '항만'은 뉴스나 경제 글에서 규모와 시설을 말할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: New port facilities were built.
phrases.nuance_ko: 배와 짐을 다루는 건물과 장비를 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Covers the buildings and equipment that handle ships and cargo.

phrases.en: Incheon is a port city.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 항만이 있어서 발전한 도시를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A city that developed around a large port.

phrases.en: I'm waiting for the boat at the harbor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '항만'보다 '항구'를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily speech, 항구 is more common than 항만.

explain_en: Large harbor as infrastructure, in trade and logistics. '항만' covers the whole set of facilities where ships come in and cargo is loaded. In daily talk '항구' is more common, while '항만' appears in news and economic writing when scale and facilities matter.

examples.en: Do you sell this snack individually too?
I want to buy single pieces, not a box.
It's individually wrapped, so it's easy to carry.
These batteries are not sold individually.
The single-piece price is a bit higher than the bundle.

examples.ko: 사탕이 낱개로 들어 있어서 나눠 먹기 좋아요.
examples.en: The candies come in single pieces, so they're easy to share.

explain: '묶음', '한 상자'의 반대 개념으로 보통 '낱개로'라는 모양으로 써요. 가게에서 물건을 하나씩 살 수 있는지 물어볼 때 유용해요.

phrases.en: This shop sells candy individually.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 하나씩 판다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say a shop sells items one at a time.

phrases.en: The snacks are individually wrapped, so they're easy to eat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하나씩 따로 싼 상품을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe products wrapped one by one.

phrases.en: Please give me just three, individually.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 살 때 필요한 만큼만 달라고 부탁하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request when buying, asking for only the amount you need.

explain_en: One unit sold separately from a set or bundle (과자 낱개) It is the opposite of '묶음' or '한 상자' and usually appears as '낱개로'. It is useful when asking in a shop whether you can buy items one at a time.

examples.en: Land prices in this neighborhood go up every year.
Land is expensive, so building a house is hard.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 서울 땅값이 또 올랐다고 했어요.
examples.en: The news said land prices in Seoul rose again.
Land near the station is much more expensive.
I want to sell before land prices fall.
The shop's rent went up too because of land prices.

explain: 집이 아니라 땅 자체의 값이에요. 집을 포함한 값은 '집값'이라고 해서 구별해요. 발음은 [땅깝]이에요.

phrases.en: A new subway station opened, so land prices went up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이고 뉴스에도 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation, often in the news.

phrases.en: Land is cheap in the countryside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비싸다'의 반대로 값이 낮을 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 비싸다, for low land prices.

phrases.en: Land prices in this neighborhood have fallen lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오르다'의 반대로 값이 떨어졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 오르다, for prices that went down.

explain_en: It is the price of the land itself, not of a house. The price including a house is '집값', so the two are distinguished. It is pronounced [땅깝].

examples.en: Check whether the taxi meter is on.
The fare was already showing on the meter.
Driver, please turn on the meter.

examples.ko: 미터기 요금과 카드 결제 금액이 같아요.
examples.en: The meter fare and the card payment amount are the same.
The meter starts from the base fare.

examples.ko: 가스 미터기 숫자를 사진으로 찍어 보냈어요.
examples.en: I took a photo of the numbers on the gas meter and sent it.

explain: 주로 택시에서 거리와 시간에 따라 요금을 보여 주는 기계를 말해요. 전기나 가스처럼 사용량을 재는 기계는 '계량기'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Driver, please turn on the meter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 택시를 탔을 때 요금 계산을 시작해 달라고 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What you say in a taxi to ask the driver to start the fare meter.

phrases.en: The meter fare came out higher than I expected.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계에 찍힌 요금을 말해요. 정해진 요금과 구분할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The fare shown on the machine, as opposed to a fixed price.

phrases.en: The traffic is bad, so the meter keeps going up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시간과 거리에 따라 요금이 늘어나는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the fare rising as time and distance add up.

explain_en: Loanword-based, everyday; fare meters like taxis or parking. It mainly means the machine in a taxi that shows the fare by distance and time. A device that measures usage, like electricity or gas, is also called '계량기'.

t90.ax: Driver, please turn on the meter.

en: amount to be borne; share to be borne

examples.ko: 이번 병원비의 본인 부담액이 얼마나 돼요?
examples.en: How much is my own share of this hospital bill?

examples.ko: 보험에 가입하면 치료비 부담액이 많이 줄어요.
examples.en: If you have insurance, the amount you pay for treatment drops a lot.
The share per person for this gathering is 50,000 won.

examples.ko: 우리는 식사 부담액을 똑같이 나눠서 내기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to split the cost of the meal equally.
I'm worried a lot about how much of the repair cost I'll have to pay.

examples.ko: 정부가 학생들의 등록금 부담액을 줄이겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: The government said it will reduce the amount students have to pay for tuition.

explain: '본인 부담액', '1인당 부담액'처럼 누가 내는지를 앞에 붙여서 자주 써요. 병원비, 보험, 모임 회비 이야기에서 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '내야 하는 돈'이라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 수술비의 본인 부담액은 보험으로 줄일 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can reduce your own share of the surgery cost with insurance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본인이 직접 내는 돈을 말할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for the amount a person pays themselves.

phrases.en: The cost per person for the trip is 200,000 won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람이 내야 하는 금액을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: It shows the amount each person has to pay.

phrases.en: As taxes rose, the amount I have to pay increased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내야 하는 돈이 많아졌을 때 '늘다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '늘다' when the amount to pay has grown.

explain_en: It is often used with a word showing who pays, as in '본인 부담액' (your own share) or '1인당 부담액' (per-person share). It comes up in talk about hospital bills, insurance and group fees. In casual speech people may also say '내야 하는 돈'.

examples.en: The share for this gathering is five thousand won.
The association members paid their share of the construction costs.
The contribution went up so much that it's a heavy burden.
The deadline for paying the contribution is next week.
The contribution is a little different for each member.
I couldn't pay my share, so I got a call.

explain: 여러 사람이나 나라가 어떤 일의 비용을 나눠 맡아서 내는 돈이에요. 정기적으로 내는 '회비'와 달리 특정 사업이나 일의 비용을 나눌 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '방위비 분담금', '재건축 분담금'으로 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: We have to pay the group's share by today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나눠 맡은 돈을 낸다는 뜻으로 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to say paying one's allotted share.

phrases.en: The news talked about the defense cost-sharing contribution.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라 사이의 비용 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in talk about costs shared between countries.

phrases.en: I want to know how much the redevelopment contribution is.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집을 새로 짓는 비용을 주민이 나눠 낼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when residents share the cost of rebuilding housing.

explain_en: Each member's assigned share of costs (모임 분담금) It is the money that several people or countries pay as their share of the cost of something. Unlike a regular '회비' (membership fee), it is for the cost of a specific project or task. In the news you often hear '방위비 분담금' and '재건축 분담금'.

t90.ax: I couldn't pay my share, so I got a call.

examples.ko: 이 과일은 모양이 예뻐서 상품성이 높아요.
examples.en: This fruit looks nice, so it has high market value.

examples.ko: 흠집이 있으면 상품성을 잃어서 싸게 팔아요.
examples.en: Items with scratches lose their sales appeal, so they're sold cheap.

examples.ko: 상품성 없는 농산물은 가공해서 쓰기도 해요.
examples.en: Produce that can't be sold as is sometimes gets processed and used.

examples.ko: 이 디자인은 상품성도 좋고 가격도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: This design sells well and the price is reasonable too.

examples.ko: 상품성은 있지만 실제로 잘 팔릴지는 모르겠어요.
examples.en: It has market potential, but I don't know if it'll really sell well.

examples.ko: 그 아이디어는 상품성에 한계가 있어 보여요.
examples.en: That idea looks limited in commercial appeal.

explain: 물건이나 아이디어가 팔릴 만한지를 볼 때 써요. '상품성이 있다/없다/떨어지다/높다'처럼 같이 써요. 농산물은 크기와 모양, 흠집 때문에 '상품성이 떨어진다'는 말을 자주 해요.

phrases.example: 이 아이디어는 상품성이 있어서 사람들이 살 것 같아요.
phrases.en: This idea has commercial value, so people would probably buy it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔릴 만하다고 좋게 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A positive evaluation that something is likely to sell.

phrases.en: Overripe fruit loses its market value.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모양이나 상태 때문에 팔기 어려워질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when looks or condition make something harder to sell.

phrases.example: 이 디자인은 상품성이 없어서 만들지 않기로 했어요.
phrases.en: This design has no commercial value, so we decided not to make it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔 가치가 없다는 분명한 평가예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A clear judgment that it isn't worth selling.

explain_en: Whether a product is good enough to sell, e.g. produce. You use it when judging whether a product or idea is good enough to sell. It combines with '있다', '없다', '떨어지다' and '높다'. For produce, people often say its '상품성이 떨어진다' because of size, shape or blemishes.

examples.en: In winter, the demand for heating rises a lot.
When prices go up, the quantity demanded usually falls.
The demand for rice this year is lower than last year.

examples.ko: 수요량을 정확히 알아야 물건을 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to know the demand exactly to make the products.
Demand for masks suddenly rose, so they sold out.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 수요량에 맞춰 빵을 구워요.
examples.en: This shop bakes bread to match the demand.

explain: 짝이 되는 말은 '공급량'이에요. 그냥 '수요'는 사려는 마음이나 필요를 넓게 말하고, '수요량'은 얼마나 필요한지 양으로 말할 때 써요. 경제 수업이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Demand for air conditioners grows in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 양이 많아질 때 '늘다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with 늘다 when the amount needed goes up.

phrases.en: When the price went up, demand dropped.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 양이 적어질 때 '줄다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use with 줄다 when the amount needed goes down.

phrases.example: 회사는 다음 달 수요량을 예측해서 물건을 만들어요.
phrases.en: The company predicts next month's demand and then makes the goods.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 얼마나 필요할지 미리 생각해 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when estimating in advance how much will be needed.

explain_en: Its counterpart is '공급량' (quantity supplied). Plain '수요' (demand) speaks broadly of the wish or need to buy, while '수요량' is for how much is needed, as an amount. It often appears in economics classes and the news.

examples.en: Korea's leading exports are semiconductors and cars.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 수출품이라서 국내에서는 팔지 않아요.
examples.en: This product is for export, so it isn't sold in Korea.

examples.ko: 수출품 포장은 훨씬 더 꼼꼼하게 해야 해요.
examples.en: Packaging for export goods has to be done much more carefully.
We are doing research to develop a new export product.

examples.ko: 수출품 검사를 통과해야 배에 실을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Export goods must pass inspection before they can be loaded onto the ship.
In this region, seaweed is an important export.

explain: 짝말은 다른 나라에서 사 오는 물건인 '수입품'이에요. '주요 수출품', '대표 수출품'처럼 말하고, 같은 뜻으로 '수출 상품'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: Cars are one of Korea's main exports.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 수출품 중 중요한 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to point out the important ones among many exports.

phrases.en: Seaweed is this region's signature export.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 나라나 지역을 대표하는 수출품을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the export that best represents a country or region.

phrases.example: 이 수출 상품은 미국에서 인기가 많아요.
phrases.en: This export product is popular in the US.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수출품'과 같은 뜻이고, 팔리는 상품이라는 느낌이 조금 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수출품, with a slightly stronger sense of a product for sale.

explain_en: Its counterpart is '수입품' (imported goods). People say '주요 수출품' (main export) or '대표 수출품' (leading export), and '수출 상품' means the same thing.

t90.ax: In this region, seaweed is an important export.

examples.en: What is the hourly wage at this shop?
I asked the boss to raise my hourly wage.

examples.ko: 시급은 낮지만 일이 편해서 계속 다녀요.
examples.en: The hourly wage is low, but the work is easy, so I keep going.

examples.ko: 시급으로 받으면 일한 시간만큼 돈이 나와요.
examples.en: If you are paid hourly, you get money for the hours you work.

examples.ko: 새로 일하는 곳은 시급 외에 식사도 줘요.
examples.en: My new workplace gives meals in addition to the hourly wage.
The work is too hard for the hourly wage.

explain: 시급은 한 시간 일하면 받는 돈이고, 월급은 한 달 일하고 받는 돈이에요. 아르바이트는 보통 시급으로 말해요. '시급이 높다', '시급을 올리다'처럼 써요. '시급하다'는 급하다는 뜻의 다른 단어예요.

phrases.en: This part-time job has a high hourly wage.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 시간에 받는 돈이 많을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the pay per hour is large.

phrases.en: That shop's hourly wage was low, so I quit.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 시간에 받는 돈이 적을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the pay per hour is small.

phrases.en: The minimum hourly wage goes up every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 법으로 정한 가장 낮은 시급을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The lowest hourly wage set by law.

explain_en: Pay per hour; common for part-time jobs. 시급 is the pay for one hour of work, and 월급 is the pay for a month. Part-time jobs are usually described by 시급. It goes with '시급이 높다' and '시급을 올리다'. '시급하다' is a different word meaning urgent.

examples.en: The professor received research funding and started the experiment.
We could not buy equipment because the research funds were short.

examples.ko: 연구비는 어디에 얼마나 썼는지 적어야 해요.
examples.en: You have to record where and how much of the research funds you spent.
We bought a new computer with the research funds.

examples.ko: 연구비 신청서를 다음 주까지 내야 해요.
examples.en: I have to submit the research funding application by next week.
Getting research funds made graduate school easier.

explain: 연구에 쓰는 돈이에요. 학교나 기관은 '연구비를 지원하다'라고 하고, 연구하는 사람은 '연구비를 받다', '연구비를 신청하다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The students applied to the school for research funds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연구하는 사람이 돈을 달라고 요청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when researchers ask for funding.

phrases.en: The company supports the university with research funds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 주는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side that gives the money.

phrases.example: 연구비를 실험 재료를 사는 데 썼어요.
phrases.en: I used the research funds to buy experiment materials.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 돈을 사용할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when spending the money received.

explain_en: Money for research; grants (연구비를 신청하다) It is money spent on research. A school or institution '연구비를 지원하다' (provides funds), while a researcher '연구비를 받다' (receives) or '연구비를 신청하다' (applies for) them.
